concepts.title: Point, Line Segment, Line and Ray
concepts.definition: A point fixes a location with no length, breadth or height; a line segment joins two points and has two endpoints; extending a segment endlessly on both sides gives a line, and extending it only one way gives a ray with one endpoint.
concepts.key_idea: Endpoint count separates the three: segment has two, ray has one, line has none.

concepts.title: Angles as Rotation
concepts.definition: An angle measures the amount of rotation between two arms joined at a vertex: opening the rotating arms wider makes a bigger angle, and the size does not depend on how long the arms are drawn.
concepts.key_idea: Angle is turning, not length: longer arms never make a bigger angle.

concepts.title: Angles on a Straight Line
concepts.definition: When a ray stands on a straight angle, the two angles on either side together make a straight angle of 180 degrees, so the unknown angle is found by subtracting the known one from 180.
concepts.key_idea: A straight line hides a fixed total: 180 degrees, which turns angle puzzles into one subtraction.

solution_steps.explain: Angles standing on a straight line fill 180 degrees together.
The unknown angle is 180 minus the known angle.

concepts.title: Measuring and Classifying Angles
concepts.section: 2.9 and 2.11 Measuring angles, types of angles
concepts.definition: A protractor measures angles in degrees; angles are classified by size as right (exactly 90 degrees), acute (smaller than a right angle), obtuse (bigger than right but less than a straight angle), straight (180 degrees) and reflex (bigger than a straight angle).
concepts.key_idea: Each angle type is a region of turning: knowing the boundaries at 90, 180 and 360 sorts every angle.
